cells.tense: A whole self is catching fire here, and the fire has not been pointed anywhere yet.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Carry something you already committed to — a way of living, a stretch of work — one more week past where doubt got a vote. No new sign. Keep at it and watch whether it holds.
cells.core:
Something is starting in you and the shape hasn't arrived. That isn't a flaw. You pick up how a system moves under its surface, how a person shifts before they say anything, and that pickup is the beginning. The plan doesn't have to land before the spark does. What holds this together is that you trust the fire and keep feeding it; the shape shows up while you walk, not before.

The next move is smaller than it looks. Carry something you already committed to — a way of living, a stretch of work — one more week past the doubt that says it's pointless. You're not checking whether you were right. You're learning whether it holds with nobody clapping. When it does, whatever lights up next already knows where to go.
cells.sheetLine: The fire doesn't need the whole plan before it lights.
cells.verb: sparking whole before it knows what for
cells.place: where the pattern is seen on its own, free of any particular thing

cells.tense: A future is being braced for here that nobody has written down yet.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Spread the whole shape of a plan out where every part can be taken in together — on paper, on a table. Let the full picture sit visible before you push it out into the world.
cells.core:
You can picture a pattern before it exists, and lately you've pictured it so hard that you're already living inside a version of this thing that hasn't happened yet. The fire got out past the shape. You're not just starting something — you're arguing for it in a room where nothing has been built. The vision stopped waiting for conditions to arrive.

Spread the whole design out where you can take in every part of it together. Let the full inventory sit visible, complete, before you push it outward. You'll notice the gap between what's actually formed and what you've been picturing. That noticing does the work. Then you can let the thing catch up to the image instead of dragging it there.

cells.tense: A doorway was crossed here a while back, and you haven't come through it.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Put every feeling about a project you started and set down onto a single page. All of them — dread, hope, boredom, wanting — with nothing crossed out. Keep the page. Nothing has to be done with any of it.
cells.core:
A spark in you lost its nerve. You caught how something worked, you knew the shape it wanted, and then the beginning stopped turning into motion. You're posted at a door that's behind you now. Not a failure. A cut wire. The charge is there and it isn't reaching the ignition, and you've been quiet about the whole thing.

Before pushing anything forward, put what you actually feel about the thing you started and dropped onto a page. All of it, nothing crossed out. You're deciding nothing. You're letting the feeling finish so it stops sitting on the connection. Once the whole charge is written down, the line goes quiet enough for the next small move to reach it.
cells.sheetLine: The spark was real, and you stopped at the doorway.
cells.verb: sparking whole before it knows what for

cells.tense: A room is being shaped by something here that nobody is claiming out loud.
cells.act: be full for an hour with what was already felt
cells.ask: Give a full hour to a thing you already finished. Use it, sit with it, let it be enough for that hour. Improve nothing. Then notice what the not-improving does.
cells.core:
You dream, and you give it another name. What a thing would look like done — its whole shape — is clear to you, and you've told yourself you're just thinking, just planning, just noticing what's obvious. The vision runs itself while you stand off to the side of it. People watch it land and have no idea anyone shaped it.

Go back to something you already finished and spend an hour with it. Not the next version, not the improved one — the one that's done and sitting there uncelebrated. Let the satisfaction land instead of reaching for what's next. The dreaming doesn't need a new permission slip. It needs you to see that shaping it was work you did.
cells.sheetLine: You give it another name, but the shaping was yours.
